source: Q144 (2026-09-23): the owner's first named correction to the Z-Anatomy reference model -- the radial nerve pathway. See PROJECT_STATE.md Q144 and data/derived/Q144_radial_nerve_audit.json for the full measurement method and table. Q145 (2026-09-23) finished the one partial correction Q144 left open (PIN/arcade-of-Frohse entry, now a bounded 3-D warp) and re-sourced the bifurcation landmark (d) from a newly found open-access cadaveric study -- see data/derived/Q145_pin_audit.json. This is the CC BY-SA layer (third_party/z-anatomy/NOTICE): no private/clinical content here.
entity: radial_n (Radial nerve) and its terminal branches, per data/nerves/brachial_plexus.json
reference_frame: atlas +Y (superior), millimetres, measured as an OFFSET from the lateral epicondyle (positive = proximal, negative = distal), where the lateral epicondyle is fit live from this same Z-Anatomy Humerus.r/.l mesh on every build (the most-lateral vertex, +X on the right / -X on the left, in the distal-most 15mm-by-Y slab) -- never a fixed number, so the correction still applies correctly if the base Z-Anatomy extraction is ever re-run. Z-Anatomy humerus length (both sides): 317.6 mm.
method: Centreline = per-Y-bin (nbins=80-150 depending on landmark) vertex centroid of the nerve mesh, sorted superior->inferior, on scripts/zanatomy zan_source.to_atlas_frame() geometry (Z-Anatomy raw FBX -> this project's atlas frame, unchanged). Bone/muscle proximity via scipy.spatial.cKDTree nearest-vertex distance; intramuscular (supinator) entry/exit via trimesh.Trimesh.contains() point-in-mesh containment (watertight check passed) rather than a nearest-vertex threshold, since a threshold is sensitive to an arbitrary cutoff. Side check: right and left Z-Anatomy geometry measured independently and confirmed to mirror exactly (both sides gave identical entry/exit/humerus-length numbers) -- one set of anchors is applied to both radial_n_r and radial_n_l/posterior_interosseous_n_r and _l.

landmarks.description: Radial nerve trunk in direct contact with the posterior humeral shaft (spiral/radial groove) -- proximal and distal extent, distance proximal to the lateral epicondyle.
landmarks.citation: Carlan D, Pratt J, Patterson JMM, Weiland AJ, Boyer MI, Gelberman RH (2007). The radial nerve in the brachium: an anatomic study in human cadavers. J Hand Surg Am 32(8):1177-82. PMID 17923300, DOI 10.1016/j.jhsa.2006.07.001.

landmarks.description: Point the radial nerve leaves the spiral groove / pierces the lateral intermuscular septum into the anterior compartment, distance proximal to the lateral epicondyle.

measured.note: distal boundary of the <5mm bone-contact zone above

cited_range.note: pooled from two independent studies' own mean+-SD

citation: Artico M, Telera S, Tiengo C, Stecco C, Macchi V, Porzionato A, Vigato E, Parenti A, De Caro R (2008). Surgical anatomy of the radial nerve at the elbow. Surg Radiol Anat 31(2):101-6. PMID 18795220, DOI 10.1007/s00276-008-0412-8. (entry into lateral intermuscular septum: 110 +/- 23 mm proximal to lateral epicondyle)

Jain RK, Champawat VS, Mandlecha P (2018). Danger zone of radial nerve in Indian population -- a cadaveric study. J Clin Orthop Trauma 10(3):531-534. PMID 31061584, DOI 10.1016/j.jcot.2018.02.006. (exit from spiral groove: 113.4 +/- 4.1 mm proximal to lateral epicondyle)

landmarks.description: Trunk position just proximal to the elbow: anterior to the humerus, between brachialis (medial) and brachioradialis (lateral).

measured.note: at the trunk's most distal centreline point (7.8mm distal to LE): X=233.9mm sits exactly between Brachialis muscle.r's X-range [211.3, 235.7] and Brachioradialis muscle.r's X-range [234.4, 271.1]; Z=-16.6mm is anterior to Humerus.r's own Z-range [-50.0, -19.9] at that level (i.e. entirely anterior to the bone).

cited_range.qualitative: anterior to humerus, becomes protected by brachialis, per Carlan et al. 2007 (PMID 17923300)

landmarks.citation: Carlan et al. 2007, PMID 17923300 (qualitative description only, no numeric target for this specific check).

landmarks.description: Level the radial nerve trunk divides into its superficial branch and the posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch), relative to the lateral epicondyle / radiocapitellar joint.

cited_range.note: 95% CI of the mean, radiocapitellar-joint(RCJ)-referenced; converted to this model's own LE frame via its own live-measured radial head offset (7.3mm distal to LE, used here as an RCJ proxy exactly as for landmark (e)/Hazani below): distal_to_LE range approx [-0.7, 5.3] mm (i.e. from ~0.7mm proximal to LE to 5.3mm distal to it).

landmarks.citation: Qawasmi F, Goss M, Shweiki F, Grindle S, Yassin M (2025). Anatomical considerations for safe retractor placement in distal biceps repair: a cadaveric study of the posterior interosseous nerve. Surg Radiol Anat 47(1):223. PMID 41053287, PMCID PMC12500735, DOI 10.1007/s00276-025-03728-3 (open access; full text retrieved via PubMed MCP). 29 fresh cadaveric upper extremities: "the radial nerve bifurcated approximately 5 +/- 3 mm proximal to the radiocapitellar joint (95% CI 2-8mm)"; the same paper's own Discussion also quotes two further studies' point estimates for this landmark (Prasartritha et al.: 13mm proximal to RCJ; Cox et al.: 10mm proximal to RCJ) -- both secondhand via Qawasmi's own citation, not independently verified here, given only as corroborating context, not as this correction's own cited target.
landmarks.status: now sourced (previously unsourced at Q144) -- measured value sits just outside the converted 95%-CI range but NOT corrected; see note
landmarks.note: Q144 could not find a numeric target for this landmark and left it unsourced; Q145 found one (Qawasmi et al. 2025, open access). Converted to this model's own LE frame, the cited range is approx [-0.7, 5.3]mm distal to LE; this model measures the bifurcation at 7.8mm (trunk end) / 8.6mm (PIN start) distal to LE -- 2.5-3.3mm outside that range, i.e. of the same order as the cited study's own reported SD (3mm) on the RCJ measurement itself, well within plausible single-specimen cadaveric variation even though it sits outside the *mean's* 95% CI. NOT corrected for two reasons, stated honestly rather than silently declared 'in range': (1) statistically this is a small, borderline discrepancy, not the >30%-of-target miss that justified correcting (e) below; (2) mechanically, correcting a bifurcation point means moving the DISTAL end of one mesh (radial_n) and the PROXIMAL ends of two others (posterior_interosseous_n, radial_n_superficial_branch) in a coordinated way so the three independently-stored objects still meet without a gap or overlap -- a materially different, riskier problem than warping a single continuous nerve's own interior path (landmark (e)'s fix), and out of this task's scope. Left for a future task if ever revisited. Artico et al. 2008 (PMID 18795220, DOI 10.1007/s00276-008-0412-8) was tried first per task instruction: its abstract describes measuring this exact division point in its Methods but does not report the number in the abstract itself, and its full text is NOT accessible (no PMC ID; PubMed MCP's own copyright-status check returned source='not_available', and a pubmed_pmc link lookup for it returned no linked PMC record) -- confirmed unavailable, not assumed, before falling back to the PubMed search that found Qawasmi et al. 2025 instead.

landmarks.description: Posterior interosseous nerve entry into supinator (proximal edge of the arcade of Frohse), distance distal to the lateral epicondyle.

measured.note: trimesh point-in-mesh containment test, PIN centreline vs Supinator.r/.l. Q145 re-checked the concern that this might be a measurement-methodology artifact rather than a real geometry gap (task's own instruction: 'the real-geometry test is nerve enters supinator mesh at X mm from LE; if the Z-Anatomy supinator itself sits where the literature puts entry, the right correction may be none') -- it is NOT a measurement artifact: the containment transition along the PIN's own centreline is a single clean in/out crossing (checked at 150 bins, no noise/multiple crossings near the boundary), and it reproduces to within 0.1mm of Q144's own 27.5mm figure. The supinator mesh's own GLOBAL Y bounding box (proximal-most vertex, not specifically along the nerve's path) sits at ~14.7mm PROXIMAL to LE -- i.e. the muscle's overall extent does reach past the cited ~42.6mm entry level in Y -- but the nerve's own actual path only enters the SOLID part of that mesh at ~27.4mm distal to LE, because in real anatomy (and evidently in this model too) the nerve travels through the open radial-tunnel space between the humeral/annular-ligament origin of supinator's superficial head and the bone before the two heads close in around it; that open-space gap is simply ~15mm shorter in this model than the cited cadaveric average. Confirmed genuine (not a mismeasurement) by cross-checking the SUPINATOR EXIT the same way: it lands within 1mm of both cited studies (81.8mm measured vs. Aggarwal's 85.4mm / Hazani-converted 81.3mm) using the identical containment method, so the method itself is not systematically biased -- only the entry side of this particular mesh sits materially proximal to where the cited cadavers place it.

landmarks.hazani_conversion_note: Hazani et al. 2008 measures from the radial head, not the lateral epicondyle -- a DIFFERENT reference point from Aggarwal et al., kept separate here rather than pooled into one cited_range (Q144's own lead-review note: 'keep the two references separate ... don't merge them into one range'). Converted using THIS model's own live-measured radial head offset (7.3mm distal to LE -- proximal-most vertex of Radius.r/.l, fit the same way lateral_epicondyle_y() fits the LE, re-verified at Q145: 7.2794mm both sides): 7.3 + 35 = 42.3mm distal to LE. The two independently-referenced targets (42.6mm direct-LE vs. 42.3mm converted-via-radial-head) agree to within 0.3mm of each other -- a good cross-check that the conversion is sound -- but are NOT averaged into a single 'cited_range' band; both are carried as separate fields and both are checked against the correction's own achieved result below.
citation: Aggarwal N, Maurya R, Tiwari V, Pathak A, Chaudhary P (2026). Surface landmark-based estimation of the posterior interosseous nerve: a cadaveric anatomical study. Hand Surg Rehabil, in press. PMID 42556533, DOI 10.1016/j.hansur.2026.102756. (lateral epicondyle to PIN entry into supinator: 4.26 cm)

Hazani R, Engineer NJ, Mowlavi A, Neumeister M, Lee WPA, Wilhelmi BJ (2008). Anatomic landmarks for the radial tunnel. Eplasty 8:e37. PMID 18668182. (deep branch of radial nerve enters supinator ~3.5 cm distal to the radial head)
landmarks.note: Q144 (Y-only warp) plateaued at ~30.4mm regardless of nominal shift, because a pure Y-shift immediately re-clips onto the Radius surface via the mandatory bone-avoidance pass: this Z-Anatomy PIN centreline runs in near-contact with the Radius (1-5mm clearance, checked Q145) for its whole course through the radial tunnel, so the real obstruction is the nerve's X/Z position relative to the bone, not just its Y level. Q145 added a bounded, additive lateral (X/Z) push AWAY from the Radius (direction computed live from the PIN's own centreline vs. the Radius surface, magnitude smoothstep-profiled 0->6.5mm->0 between the same bifurcation/entry/exit anchors used for the Y-shift, hard-capped at 8mm) applied BEFORE the existing bone-avoidance pass, then re-ran that pass (now also guarding Ulna and Humerus, not just Radius). Parameter sweep (see data/derived/Q145_pin_audit.json) found a wide, stable plateau (push 6.2-6.6mm x Y-shift -11 to -14mm all land within 42.5-44.2mm, not a knife's-edge single point) and (push=6.5mm, Y-shift=-13mm) sits at its centre, giving achieved entry 42.55mm -- within 0.05mm of Aggarwal's 42.6mm target and 0.25mm of Hazani's independently-converted 42.3mm. Post-correction re-check: 0 vertices inside Radius/Ulna/Humerus on either side (both were already 0 for Ulna/Humerus even under the old Y-only warp; Radius was the only bone the Y-only warp ever penetrated), exit unchanged at 81.8mm (still within both cited ranges), mesh topology/connectivity unchanged (main_frac 1.0 both before and after, trivially guaranteed since only vertex positions move).

landmarks.description: Posterior interosseous nerve exit from supinator (distal edge of the superficial part of supinator), distance distal to the lateral epicondyle.

measured.note: same containment test, distal-most contained centreline point

citation: Aggarwal N, Maurya R, Tiwari V, Pathak A, Chaudhary P (2026). PMID 42556533, DOI 10.1016/j.hansur.2026.102756. (lateral epicondyle to PIN exit from supinator: 8.54 cm)
Hazani R et al. (2008). PMID 18668182. (PIN exits supinator ~7.4-7.5 cm distal to the radial head -> ~8.1 cm from the lateral epicondyle on this model's own frame)
landmarks.note: Kept as a FIXED (zero-shift) anchor for the entry correction's warp, since it already matches the literature (measured 81.8mm vs. cited 77-90mm).

landmarks.description: Superficial branch running deep to brachioradialis for most of the forearm, emerging from under it in the distal forearm.

measured.note: Nearest-vertex distance from the superficial branch centreline to Brachioradialis.r stays under ~6mm from the elbow to within ~10mm proximal to the radial styloid, i.e. consistently close to/deep to the muscle throughout -- but a nearest-VERTEX distance cannot itself distinguish deep (posterior) from superficial (anterior) position, so the specific emergence transition point could not be independently verified against the cited distance with the available geometry proxy.

cited_range.reference_point: proximal to the radial styloid, not the lateral epicondyle

landmarks.citation: Beldner S, Zlotolow DA, Melone CP, Agnes AM, Jones MH (2005). Anatomy of the lateral antebrachial cutaneous and superficial radial nerves in the forearm: a cadaveric and clinical study. J Hand Surg Am 30(6):1226-30. PMID 16344180, DOI 10.1016/j.jhsa.2005.07.004. (SRN deep to brachioradialis until 9 cm proximal to the radial styloid, where it becomes superficial)
landmarks.status: qualitatively consistent -- transition point unsourced by available proxy, not corrected

correction.method: Q145: a bounded, smooth (C1 cubic-smoothstep) 3-D warp -- Q144's own Y-only (atlas superior-inferior) warp, UNCHANGED in mechanism, plus a new additive X/Z ('lateral_push', below) component, followed by the same mandatory bone-avoidance safety pass. No topology change (same vertex/face count and connectivity) in either component. Y-anchors, as (offset_mm_from_lateral_epicondyle, shift_mm), sorted ascending: the PIN's own measured proximal origin at the trunk bifurcation (-8.6, 0 -- item d, left unmoved, see that landmark's own Q145 note on why its own small discrepancy is not corrected here), the measured supinator entry (-27.5, -13.0 -- item e_pin_supinator_entry; Q144 used -12.0, Q145 retuned to -13.0 as part of the joint (Y-shift, lateral-push) parameter search -- see that landmark's own note), and the measured supinator exit (-81.8, 0 -- item e_pin_supinator_exit, within cited range, left unmoved). Outside the outermost anchors the shift is clamped to that anchor's own value (0 at both ends), so only the PIN mesh between the bifurcation and the supinator exit is touched -- unchanged from Q144.

lateral_push.note: Q145: additive displacement in the atlas X/Z (horizontal) plane only, magnitude smoothstep-profiled by the same bump_warp_y() interpolation used for the Y-anchors above (0 at the bifurcation and supinator-exit anchors, a 6.5mm plateau across the entry region, hard-clamped to 8mm regardless of anchor values -- the explicit 'max displacement cap' this task asked for). DIRECTION is never baked into this file: scripts/zanatomy/apply_corrections.py's own _bone_repulsion_direction() computes it LIVE, per Y-level, from THIS build's own PIN centreline vs. its own Radius mesh surface (nearest-surface-point ray, pointing away from the bone -- same live-fit philosophy as lateral_epicondyle_y()), so this still applies correctly if the base Z-Anatomy extraction is ever regenerated. Why needed: Q144's Y-only warp plateaued at ~30-36mm regardless of nominal shift because this model's PIN centreline runs in 1-5mm clearance of the Radius for its whole course through the radial tunnel (checked empirically, Q145), so any further distal Y-shift was immediately re-clipped onto the bone by the safety pass below; pushing the same region sideways, away from the bone, before that pass runs removes the obstruction instead of just re-hitting it. (push_mm, y_shift_mm) = (6.5, -13.0) was chosen from the centre of a wide, stable parameter-space plateau (push 6.2-6.6mm x y-shift -11 to -14mm all land within 42.5-44.2mm entry, not a knife-edge single point -- see data/derived/Q145_pin_audit.json's own sweep table), not the single best-fit point, so the result is robust to small re-measurement of the anchors on a future re-extraction.

correction.avoid_penetration_note: Q144: a pure Y-shift, checked empirically, put ~11% of the corrected PIN's own vertices inside the Z-Anatomy Radius mesh (the PIN wraps tightly around the radial neck, exactly where a Y-only warp is most likely to clip a bone whose cross-section is not constant along Y) -- scripts/zanatomy/apply_corrections.py's own _push_off_bones() projects any such vertex to the nearest bone surface plus a 1mm clearance along the point-to-surface ray (NOT the face normal -- checked empirically that this mesh's face normals point inward), after the full warp, before shipping. Q145 widened this list from just Radius to also guard Ulna and Humerus (both already measured at 0 penetration under Q144's Y-only warp and remain 0 under the new 3-D warp -- included for defense-in-depth given the larger, multi-axis displacement, not because either was ever observed to be violated). Re-checked post-Q145-fix: 0 vertices inside Radius/Ulna/Humerus on either side; achieved entry 42.55mm (both sides, confirmed mirror-exact) -- see data/derived/Q145_pin_audit.json.
correction.procedural_badge_note: course corrected per Aggarwal et al. 2026 (PMID 42556533) and Hazani et al. 2008 (PMID 18668182): posterior interosseous nerve entry into supinator (arcade of Frohse) moved along a bounded 3-D (Y plus lateral X/Z, away from the radius) warp from the measured 27.5mm to 42.55mm distal to the lateral epicondyle, matching Aggarwal's 42.6mm target to within 0.05mm and Hazani's independently radial-head-converted 42.3mm target to within 0.25mm; the nerve's supinator exit (81.8mm) and bone clearance (0 vertices inside Radius/Ulna/Humerus) are unchanged and unaffected -- see data/corrections/zanatomy/radial_n.json (Q144/Q145) and data/derived/Q145_pin_audit.json.
